The letter establishes the course of study for the student and costs the Attaché will pay on behalf of the student. Covered costs include tuition, mandatory fees, compulsory curriculum charges, health/accident insurance, and medical/dental costs incurred beyond insurance coverage. Payment on behalf of the students are contingent on them obtaining a J-1 visa, and enrolling fulltime in a program leading to a degree in the indicated course of study. Texas A&M must provide the Attache’s Office an official transcript for each semester supported and must notify them if the student’s course load drops below full-time.  Except in trauma emergency situations, the Attache’s Office requires that supported medical treatments be incurred at a non-profit, university, or government supported facility.  They further require advanced approval for dental expenses and exclude precious metals from being used in dental treatments. Texas A&M is to directly bill the Attache’s Office twice per year with an invoice that is signed and certified by Texas A&M and that indicates the number of credit hours in which the student is enrolled.
